summary: Bounded current-main FidelityManager mining found no new practical non-duplicate source gap after live lane/PR archaeology. The concrete mutable-facade capability gap is already HG-FIDELITY-MANAGER-STATE-ENCAPSULATION; open-shaped PolicyConfig/PolicyInputs are already HG-FIDELITY-CONFIG-CLOSED-SHAPE; configured capacity ceiling/exactness and rejected-step/config/callback atomicity already have dedicated retained/proposed lineages. No speculative metric-counter-overflow lane was created because a server-local diagnostic counter reaching IEEE-754 precision loss is not a demonstrated practical Hero-Gate defect.
evidence: Current main ec7755717c9512b8418e2cfc77f0da69610ea9ae exposes config/_states/_metrics on ManagerImpl; HG-FIDELITY-MANAGER-STATE-ENCAPSULATION already owns that exact capability boundary and proposes closure-private state/frozen facade semantics.
HG-FIDELITY-CONFIG-CLOSED-SHAPE already owns unknown-key rejection for all recognized PolicyConfig and PolicyInputs fields, including safety-budget and observation/relevance typos.

HG-BACKFILL-FIDELITY-CAPACITY-EXACTNESS and PR #419 own numeric exactness/project-owned registration ceiling, while PRs #274/#335 and retained Fidelity lineage own malformed-input no-execute, rejected-step atomicity, callback transactionality, reentrancy, and config copy/freeze behavior.

A repository PR search found no dedicated metric-counter overflow work, but no practical lifetime/repro demonstrating that diagnostic counters can approach the IEEE-754 exactness boundary was found; creating a lane would violate the project's measured-gap and no-hypothetical-overengineering rules.

metadata.recommendedNext: Leave Fidelity sequencing to its existing retained/proposed lineages and move idle capacity to a different unclaimed foundation shard.
